evidence: ASK: instruction.md:1-15 asks for a multi-user recruiting workspace with a server-backed pipeline board (one-stage moves, shared hand order, interview capacity, 409 stale-move refusal naming who, all-or-nothing bulk moves, own-move undo), live updates within 15 s that preserve typing/focus/scroll, paged conversations with per-person unread/seen and drafts surviving reload and session end, candidate sign-in with redaction, Node/Express/SQLite persistence across restarts (rules.md sections 1-9). environment/Dockerfile:17-23 ships an empty /app (only .gitkeep), so this is a from-scratch build, not a trivial tweak; the golden is ~1,400 lines across server and three client modules. SMALLEST SUBMISSION ANALYSIS (skill quality-checks.md:34): (a) static page/mock - render gate (gates/render/judge.toml:23) requires a wrong password to leave the visitor signed out and a correct one to show a usable workspace, and the constraints gate (gates/constraints/judge.toml:23) requires a job and candidate created through UI to appear in a NEW independent empty browser context for the Observer, explicitly excluding 'a static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app'; score.py:41,48 gives 0.0 unless both gates pass. (b) single CRUD screen with auth + server persistence for jobs/candidates - passes gates but in Functional can plausibly earn only hro_job_open 0.5 + hro_add_candidate 0.5 + hro_add_email_rules 1 = 2/59.5 = 0.034, below the functional floor 0.05 (scoring.toml:11, score.py:47-48 strict '>'), so reward 0.0. hro_anonymous (1.5) needs successful controls for move/undo/message requests the CRUD app lacks; hro_restart (1.5) needs seeded stage order and Noor's seeded internal note shown, which a CRUD screen lacks. (c) Clearing the floor requires e.g. a stage board with one-stage moves (hro_move_one_stage 1.5) or similar real features; at that point the submission is genuine partial build work and shaped partial reward is the intended design. Highest-weight criteria (hro_stale_refused 2.5, hro_live_board 2.5, hro_candidate_private 2.5, undo/bulk 2 each, polish live-preservation 3 each) target the hard behaviours, so a stub cannot approach a meaningful score. RUNTIME: raw-evidence-index scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; the scripted golden observations (results/workspace.json, hashes verified) show the golden implements the hard rules but say nothing about a weak app's reward. The stub-exclusion conclusion therefore rests on source arithmetic and judge-prompt wording, not on a measured weak-app run.
counterexample: Tried both directions. Plausible broken app that could pass: a login + jobs/candidates CRUD with SQLite persistence and a nice style passes both gates; Functional ~0.034 < 0.05 floor so reward 0 by score.py, unless a lenient judge credits hro_restart or hro_anonymous without the required controls (unmeasured; would lift Functional to ~0.06 and expose visual likert credit up to 0.2). Conforming alternative that could fail: none found for this row - the ask does not mandate drag, layout, routes or theme, and gates accept any staff workspace with navigation and readable content. No credible Fail.
